Panathinaikos.q: Ajax were in front inside five minutes of the 1971 European Cup final at Wembley. Who headed in that opening goal against Panathinaikos?
Panathinaikos.hint: Dick van Dijk headed in a Piet Keizer cross in the fifth minute, and Arie Haan added Ajax's second in the 87th as they won 2-0.

Panathinaikos.q: Which Hungarian great was in the Panathinaikos dugout for the 1971 European Cup final?
Panathinaikos.hint: Ferenc Puskás arrived in Athens in 1970 and took Panathinaikos to Wembley, still the only European Cup final reached by a Greek club.

Panathinaikos.q: Panathinaikos lost the first leg of the 1971 European Cup semi-final 4-1 away, then won the return 3-0 to go through on away goals. Who did they knock out?
Panathinaikos.hint: Red Star Belgrade were beaten 3-0 in Athens after winning 4-1 in Belgrade, the tie finishing 4-4 with Panathinaikos through on away goals.

Panathinaikos.q: Which English club did Panathinaikos eliminate on away goals in the quarter-finals of that 1970-71 European Cup run?
Panathinaikos.hint: Panathinaikos drew 1-1 at Goodison Park and 0-0 at home to knock out Everton on away goals.

Panathinaikos.q: Who finished as the leading scorer of the 1970-71 European Cup with 10 goals?
Panathinaikos.hint: Antonis Antoniadis top-scored in the 1970-71 European Cup with 10 goals as Panathinaikos reached the final.

Panathinaikos.q: Beaten finalists Panathinaikos took Ajax's place in the 1971 Intercontinental Cup after the Dutch champions declined to play it. Which South American side beat them over two legs?
Panathinaikos.hint: Uruguay's Nacional drew 1-1 in Greece and won the second leg 2-1 in Montevideo to take the 1971 Intercontinental Cup.

Panathinaikos.q: Panathinaikos' ground on Leoforos Alexandras, open since 1922, is named after Apostolos Nikolaidis. Who was he?
o: A leading club athlete who later served as club president
The architect who designed the ground
The mayor of Athens who donated the land
The man who founded Panathinaikos in 1908
Panathinaikos.hint: Apostolos Nikolaidis was a star athlete of the Panathinaikos club who went on to serve as its president; the club was founded in 1908 by Giorgos Kalafatis.

Panathinaikos.q: Panathinaikos won 1-0 away to Ajax in the first leg of the 1996 Champions League semi-final. Who scored the 87th-minute goal in Amsterdam?
Panathinaikos.hint: Krzysztof Warzycha struck in the 87th minute on 3 April 1996 for a 1-0 win at Ajax, though Panathinaikos lost the return 3-0 in Athens.

Panathinaikos.q: Which English club ended the Panathinaikos run at the semi-final stage of the 1984-85 European Cup?
Panathinaikos.hint: Liverpool won both legs against Panathinaikos in 1985 and went on to the Heysel final against Juventus.

Panathinaikos.q: What is the meeting between Panathinaikos and Olympiacos traditionally known as?
o: The Derby of the Eternal Enemies
The Derby of the Two Harbours
Panathinaikos.hint: The Panathinaikos-Olympiacos fixture is known as the Derby of the Eternal Enemies, Greek football's fiercest rivalry.

Panathinaikos.q: Which coach led Panathinaikos to the league and cup double in 2003-04?
Panathinaikos.hint: Israeli coach Itzhak Shum won the 2003-04 double, and was replaced by Zdeněk Ščasný early the following season.

Panathinaikos.q: Panathinaikos completed that 2004 double by winning the Greek Cup final 3-1. Who did they beat?
Panathinaikos.hint: Panathinaikos beat Olympiacos 3-1 in the 2004 Greek Cup final at Nea Smyrni to add the cup to the title.

Panathinaikos.q: Nikos Nioplias was appointed in December 2009 and went on to win the double that season. Which manager had he replaced?
Panathinaikos.hint: Henk ten Cate was sacked in December 2009 after Panathinaikos lost top spot to Olympiacos, and Nioplias took over and won the double.

Panathinaikos.q: On the way to the 2009-10 double, Panathinaikos also knocked an Italian side out of the Europa League 6-4 on aggregate. Which one?
Panathinaikos.hint: Panathinaikos beat Roma 3-2 in Athens and 3-2 in Rome in February 2010 to reach the last 16.

Panathinaikos.q: Who was Panathinaikos' leading league scorer in the 2009-10 double season, with 23 goals?
Panathinaikos.hint: Djibril Cissé, signed from Marseille in 2009, scored 23 league goals and 29 in all competitions in the double season.

Panathinaikos.q: Who is Panathinaikos' all-time leading goalscorer?
Panathinaikos.hint: Polish striker Krzysztof Warzycha joined in 1989, stayed 15 years and finished as the club's all-time top scorer.

Panathinaikos.q: Mimis Domazos, captain at Wembley in 1971, briefly left Panathinaikos late in his career before returning to retire there. Where did he go?
Panathinaikos.hint: After nearly two decades at Panathinaikos, Domazos had a short spell at AEK Athens from 1978 before returning to end his career with the Greens.

Panathinaikos.q: The Panathinaikos nickname "to Trifylli" comes from what on the club badge?
Panathinaikos.hint: The three-leaf clover, or shamrock, was proposed as the club's emblem in 1918 and gave Panathinaikos the nickname "to Trifylli".

Panathinaikos.q: Panathinaikos stunned Ajax with a 1-0 win in Amsterdam in the first leg of the 1995-96 Champions League semi-final. Who scored the 87th-minute winner?
Panathinaikos.hint: Krzysztof Warzycha chipped in the only goal in the 87th minute at the Amsterdam Olympic Stadium on 3 April 1996, ending an 18-match unbeaten European run for Ajax.

Panathinaikos.q: Panathinaikos lost their opening match of the 1995-96 Champions League group stage 1-0 away, only for UEFA to annul the result and expel their hosts for trying to bribe the referee. Which club was thrown out?
Panathinaikos.hint: Dynamo Kyiv's 1-0 win over Panathinaikos on 13 September 1995 was annulled after they were expelled for attempting to bribe referee Antonio López Nieto, with Danish side AaB taking their place in the group.

Panathinaikos.q: Which side did Panathinaikos eliminate 3-0 on aggregate in the 1995-96 Champions League quarter-finals?
Panathinaikos.hint: Panathinaikos drew 0-0 in Warsaw and then beat Legia Warsaw 3-0 at the Athens Olympic Stadium on 20 March 1996, Krzysztof Warzycha scoring twice and Juan José Borrelli adding the third.

Panathinaikos.q: Who was the manager who led Panathinaikos to both the Greek title and the Champions League semi-finals in 1995-96?
Panathinaikos.hint: Argentine Juan Ramón Rocha was in charge as Panathinaikos won the 1995-96 Greek championship and reached the Champions League semi-finals, where they lost 3-1 on aggregate to Ajax.

Panathinaikos.q: Panathinaikos beat Arsenal 1-0 in Athens in the 2001-02 Champions League group stage. Who headed in the only goal?
Panathinaikos.hint: Giorgos Karagounis headed the winner in the 25th minute at the Leoforos Alexandras Stadium on 26 September 2001 as Panathinaikos beat Arsenal 1-0.

Panathinaikos.q: Arsenal and Panathinaikos both went through from the same group in the 2001-02 Champions League first group stage. Which club finished top of it?
Panathinaikos.hint: Panathinaikos won Group C with 12 points from four wins, three clear of Arsenal, having beaten them 1-0 in Athens before losing 2-1 at Highbury.

Panathinaikos.q: Nikos Liberopoulos opened the scoring as Panathinaikos drew 2-2 with eventual champions Real Madrid in Athens in March 2002. Who scored their second goal?
Panathinaikos.hint: Defender Giannis Goumas put Panathinaikos 2-1 ahead in the 64th minute at the Leoforos Alexandras on 20 March 2002, before Javier Portillo levelled late for a Real Madrid side that went on to win the trophy.

Panathinaikos.q: Panathinaikos won the home leg of their 2001-02 Champions League quarter-final 1-0 through an Angelos Basinas penalty, but still went out. Who beat them?
Panathinaikos.hint: Barcelona lost 1-0 in Athens on 3 April 2002 but won the return 3-1 at Camp Nou to advance 3-2 on aggregate.

Panathinaikos.q: Krzysztof Warzycha, still Panathinaikos's all-time leading scorer, joined the club in December 1989 from which Polish side?
Panathinaikos.hint: Warzycha arrived from Ruch Chorzów in December 1989, having just won the Polish championship and finished as the league's top scorer with them.

Panathinaikos.q: Robert Jarni wound up his playing career with a half-season at Panathinaikos in 2002. Which club did he join them from?
Panathinaikos.hint: Jarni signed for Panathinaikos from Spanish side Las Palmas on 30 January 2002 on a deal until the end of the season, then retired aged 33.

Panathinaikos.q: Djibril Cissé signed for Panathinaikos in June 2009. Which club did they buy him from?
Panathinaikos.hint: Panathinaikos paid Marseille a reported €8 million for Cissé on 25 June 2009, handing him a four-year contract.

Panathinaikos.q: Djibril Cissé left Panathinaikos in July 2011 after two prolific seasons in Athens. Where did he go next?
Panathinaikos.hint: Cissé joined Lazio on 12 July 2011 for a reported €5.8 million, having scored 55 goals in 89 games for Panathinaikos.

Panathinaikos.q: Panathinaikos completed the 2010 domestic double by winning the Greek Cup final 1-0 at the Olympic Stadium. Who did they beat?
Panathinaikos.hint: Sebastián Leto's 63rd-minute goal beat Aris 1-0 in the Greek Cup final on 24 April 2010, in front of 48,926 at the Athens Olympic Stadium.

Panathinaikos.q: Which coach, appointed in December 2009 after Henk ten Cate was dismissed, led Panathinaikos to the 2010 league and cup double?
Panathinaikos.hint: Nikos Nioplias took charge on 8 December 2009 and steered Panathinaikos to the Super League title and the Greek Cup — the club's eighth double and, so far, its last.

Panathinaikos.q: Who wore the captain's armband for Panathinaikos in the 2010 Greek Cup final that sealed the double?
Panathinaikos.hint: Gilberto Silva, the Brazil World Cup winner signed from Arsenal in 2008, captained the side that beat Aris 1-0; Giorgos Karagounis came on as a substitute.

Panathinaikos.q: Giorgos Karagounis left Panathinaikos in 2003 and returned to the club four years later. Which side did he join on leaving?
Panathinaikos.hint: Karagounis moved to Inter Milan in 2003, spent two seasons at Benfica from 2005, and came back to Panathinaikos in 2007 for a five-year second spell.

Panathinaikos.q: Panathinaikos knocked a French club out of Champions League qualifying on penalties in August 2023 after a 2-2 aggregate draw. Which one?
Panathinaikos.hint: Panathinaikos beat Marseille 5-3 on penalties on 15 August 2023, Fotis Ioannidis having forced extra time with a spot-kick deep into stoppage time at the Stade Vélodrome.

Panathinaikos.q: In August 2024 Panathinaikos went out of Europa League qualifying 13-12 on penalties, after a UEFA-record 34 spot-kicks were taken. Who beat them?
Panathinaikos.hint: Ajax won the third-qualifying-round shoot-out 13-12 on 15 August 2024, the longest in UEFA club competition history, with goalkeeper Remko Pasveer saving five penalties and converting his own.

Olympiacos.q: Which coach was in charge of Olympiacos for their 2013-14 Champions League campaign?
Olympiacos.hint: Míchel, the former Real Madrid and Spain midfielder, was Olympiacos head coach in 2013-14 and took them to the round of 16.

Olympiacos.q: Olympiacos beat Manchester United 2-0 at the Karaiskakis Stadium in the first leg of the 2013-14 Champions League round of 16. Who opened the scoring before half-time?
Olympiacos.hint: Alejandro Domínguez turned in Giannis Maniatis's effort on 38 minutes to start the 2-0 win on 25 February 2014.

Olympiacos.q: In Olympiacos's 2-0 win over Manchester United in the 2013-14 round of 16, the second goal was scored by a forward spending the season on loan from Arsenal. Who was he?
Olympiacos.hint: Costa Rica forward Joel Campbell, on loan at Olympiacos from Arsenal, made it 2-0 on 54 minutes.

Olympiacos.q: Olympiacos carried a 2-0 lead to Old Trafford in the 2013-14 round of 16 second leg but lost 3-0. Whose hat-trick knocked them out?
Olympiacos.hint: Robin van Persie scored all three — a penalty, a close-range finish and a free-kick — as Manchester United went through 3-2 on aggregate on 19 March 2014.

Olympiacos.q: Olympiacos won 3-2 away to Arsenal in the Champions League group stage in September 2015. Which Arsenal goalkeeper, picked ahead of Petr Čech, dropped a corner over his own line?
Olympiacos.hint: Arsène Wenger selected David Ospina instead of Petr Čech, and Ospina's errors — including a corner spilled over his line — helped Olympiacos win 3-2 at the Emirates.

Olympiacos.q: From which German club did Olympiacos sign Kostas Fortounis in 2014?
Olympiacos.hint: Fortounis spent 2011 to 2014 at 1. FC Kaiserslautern before joining Olympiacos in July 2014.

Olympiacos.q: Before moving to Germany, Kostas Fortounis broke into the Greek top flight with which club?
Olympiacos.hint: Fortounis scored his first Super League goal for Asteras Tripolis in 2010-11, the season before he left for Kaiserslautern.

Olympiacos.q: Who captained Olympiacos in the 2024 UEFA Conference League final and lifted the trophy?
Olympiacos.hint: Kostas Fortounis, Olympiacos captain since August 2018, wore the armband for the 1-0 win over Fiorentina.

Olympiacos.q: Vasilis Torosidis left Olympiacos in January 2013 to join which Italian club?
Olympiacos.hint: Torosidis joined Roma in January 2013 and spent three and a half seasons there before moving to Bologna in 2016.

Olympiacos.q: Vasilis Torosidis scored the winner in Greece's first ever World Cup victory, at South Africa 2010. Who were the opponents?
Olympiacos.hint: Torosidis struck on 71 minutes as Greece beat 10-man Nigeria 2-1 on 17 June 2010 for their first win at a World Cup.

Olympiacos.q: Yaya Touré's first spell at Olympiacos began in 2005, when he arrived from which Ukrainian club?
Olympiacos.hint: Touré signed from Metalurh Donetsk in 2005, won the Greek league and cup double, then left for Monaco in the summer of 2006.

Olympiacos.q: Yaya Touré returned to Olympiacos in September 2018 but was released three months later after only five appearances. Who was the coach who left him out?
Olympiacos.hint: Touré failed to convince Pedro Martins and his contract was terminated by mutual agreement in December 2018.

Olympiacos.q: Olympiacos hired Pedro Martins in 2018 from which Portuguese club?
Olympiacos.hint: Martins had managed Vitória de Guimarães for two seasons before taking over at Olympiacos, where he won three consecutive Greek titles.

Olympiacos.q: Olympiacos knocked Arsenal out of the 2019-20 Europa League on away goals, winning 2-1 at the Emirates with a goal in the 119th minute. Who scored it?
Olympiacos.hint: Youssef El Arabi struck in the 119th minute on 27 February 2020 to send Olympiacos through 2-2 on away goals.

Olympiacos.q: Tottenham led 2-0 at the Karaiskakis in Olympiacos's opening game of the 2019-20 Champions League group stage before the hosts drew 2-2. Who scored the equaliser from the penalty spot?
Olympiacos.hint: Mathieu Valbuena converted the penalty on 54 minutes after Daniel Podence had pulled one back just before half-time.

Olympiacos.q: Which coach, appointed only in February 2024, led Olympiacos to the Conference League title that season?
Olympiacos.hint: José Luis Mendilibar took charge on 11 February 2024, months after winning the Europa League with Sevilla, and lifted the Conference League in May.

Olympiacos.q: Who scored the goal that won Olympiacos the 2024 Conference League final against Fiorentina?
Olympiacos.hint: Ayoub El Kaabi headed in Santiago Hezze's cross in the 116th minute to settle the final 1-0 in Athens.

Olympiacos.q: Which club did Olympiacos beat 6-2 on aggregate in the semi-finals on the way to the 2024 Conference League title?
Olympiacos.hint: Ayoub El Kaabi scored a hat-trick in a 4-2 win at Villa Park and both goals in the 2-0 second leg as Olympiacos beat Aston Villa 6-2.

Olympiacos.q: Where was the 2024 UEFA Conference League final, won by Olympiacos, played?
Olympiacos.hint: The final was staged at the Agia Sophia Stadium, AEK Athens's ground, so Olympiacos won Greece's first European trophy in their own city but not at their own stadium.

Olympiacos.q: What is the Olympiacos v Panathinaikos fixture commonly called in English?
Olympiacos.hint: Olympiacos v Panathinaikos is known as the Derby of the Eternal Enemies, a rivalry rooted in working-class Piraeus, where Olympiacos were founded in 1925, against the old Athenian society of Panathinaikos in the city centre.

Olympiacos.q: Olympiacos supporters call the club 'Thrylos'. What does the nickname mean?
Olympiacos.hint: Thrylos translates as 'The Legend', the club's best-known nickname alongside Erythrolefkoi, the Red-Whites.

Olympiacos.q: Olympiacos demolished and rebuilt Karaiskakis Stadium in just 14 months, moving into the new ground in which year?
Olympiacos.hint: The rebuilt Karaiskakis Stadium opened in 2004, in time to stage football at the Athens Olympics; Olympiacos' first competitive match there was a 2-1 win over Kallithea on 19 September 2004.

Olympiacos.q: Olympiacos' Karaiskakis Stadium takes its name from Georgios Karaiskakis. Who was he?
o: A commander of the Greek War of Independence
A shipping magnate who paid for the ground
Olympiacos.hint: Georgios Karaiskakis was a military commander and national hero of the Greek War of Independence who was mortally wounded in the Neo Faliro area where the stadium now stands.

Olympiacos.q: In February 1981, 21 Olympiacos fans were crushed to death leaving Karaiskakis Stadium after a 6-0 win over AEK Athens. Which gate gave the tragedy its name?
Olympiacos.hint: The disaster of 8 February 1981 happened at Gate 7, and the club's main supporters' association still carries that name in memory of the 21 who died.

Olympiacos.q: Olympiacos' run of seven straight championships began in 1996-97, and one manager delivered the first three before leaving in November 1999. Who was he?
Olympiacos.hint: Dusan Bajevic won the 1996-97, 1997-98 and 1998-99 titles before departing in November 1999; Ioannis Matzourakis, Takis Lemonis and Oleg Protasov saw out the rest of the seven-year run.

Olympiacos.q: Before taking charge at Olympiacos in 1996, Dusan Bajevic had already won four Greek championships as manager of which club?
Olympiacos.hint: Bajevic won four league titles at AEK Athens between 1989 and 1994 before crossing to Olympiacos, where he won three more in a row and later added the 2004-05 championship.

Olympiacos.q: Olympiacos' seven-in-a-row ended when they were beaten to the 2003-04 title. Which club took it?
Olympiacos.hint: Panathinaikos won the 2003-04 championship, ending Olympiacos' seven consecutive titles from 1996-97 to 2002-03.

Olympiacos.q: Stelios Giannakopoulos was at Olympiacos for all seven titles of the 1997-2003 run, then left in May 2003 for which Premier League club?
Olympiacos.hint: Giannakopoulos signed for Bolton Wanderers on 28 May 2003 after winning the Greek championship in every one of his seven seasons at Olympiacos, and stayed in England until 2008.

Olympiacos.q: Olympiacos paid a reported 10.8 million pounds in the summer of 1999 for the Brazilian playmaker Giovanni. Which club did they buy him from?
Olympiacos.hint: Giovanni joined Olympiacos from Barcelona in 1999, three years after the Catalans had signed him from Santos.

Olympiacos.q: Giovanni spent six seasons at Olympiacos, from 1999 until 2005. How many Greek league titles did he win there?
Olympiacos.hint: Giovanni won five championships with Olympiacos — 1999-2000, 2000-01, 2001-02, 2002-03 and 2004-05 — missing out only in 2003-04, the season he finished as the league's top scorer with 21 goals.

Olympiacos.q: Predrag Djordjevic and Stelios Giannakopoulos arrived at Olympiacos together in 1996 from the same Greek club. Which one?
Olympiacos.hint: Dusan Bajevic signed both Djordjevic and Giannakopoulos from Paniliakos in 1996, and both went on to win every title of the seven-year run.

Olympiacos.q: Predrag Djordjevic played 13 seasons at Olympiacos between 1996 and 2009. How many Greek championships did he collect?
Olympiacos.hint: Djordjevic won twelve Greek titles at Olympiacos, from 1996-97 through to 2008-09, and also holds the club's record for appearances in European competition.

Olympiacos.q: Rivaldo signed for Olympiacos in July 2004. Which club did he join them from?
Olympiacos.hint: Rivaldo joined Olympiacos on 22 July 2004 from Cruzeiro, where he had spent only around two months after leaving AC Milan.

Olympiacos.q: Olympiacos led 1-0 at Anfield in December 2004 through a curling free-kick, before Liverpool won 3-1 with a late Steven Gerrard strike. Who scored that free-kick?
Olympiacos.hint: Rivaldo bent the free-kick into the Kop end to put Olympiacos ahead on 8 December 2004, before Sinama Pongolle, Mellor and Gerrard turned the group tie around and sent Liverpool on their way to Istanbul.

Olympiacos.q: Rivaldo left Olympiacos in 2007 after three league titles and signed immediately for which club, a move that did not go down well in Piraeus?
Olympiacos.hint: Rivaldo joined AEK Athens on 29 May 2007 straight from Olympiacos, having won the Greek championship in each of his three seasons at the club.

Olympiacos.q: Olympiacos reached the Champions League quarter-finals in 1998-99, losing 2-1 away and drawing 1-1 at home to go out 3-2 on aggregate. Which club knocked them out?
Olympiacos.hint: Juventus beat Olympiacos 2-1 in Turin and drew the return 1-1 to win the 1998-99 quarter-final 3-2 on aggregate.

Olympiacos.q: Olympiacos won the 2024 UEFA Europa Conference League final 1-0 against Fiorentina with a header in the 116th minute. Who scored it?
Olympiacos.hint: Ayoub El Kaabi headed in Santiago Hezze's cross in the 116th minute at the Agia Sophia Stadium in Athens, making Olympiacos the first Greek club to win a European trophy.

Leicester City.q: Leicester City's first ever Champions League goal came inside five minutes of their debut in the competition, a 3-0 win away at Club Brugge in September 2016. Who scored it?
Leicester City.hint: Marc Albrighton scored Leicester's first ever Champions League goal in the fifth minute at the Jan Breydel Stadium in September 2016, with Riyad Mahrez adding the other two in a 3-0 win.

Leicester City.q: In the last-16 second leg against Sevilla in March 2017, Kasper Schmeichel gave away a penalty and then saved it. Which Sevilla player did he deny from the spot?
Leicester City.hint: Schmeichel brought down Vitolo to concede the penalty but then saved Steven N'Zonzi's spot-kick low to his left, protecting the 2-0 lead that took Leicester through 3-2 on aggregate.

Leicester City.q: Claudio Ranieri was sacked by Leicester in February 2017, less than 24 hours after which match?
o: A 1-0 FA Cup defeat at Millwall
A 2-1 defeat away at Sevilla in the Champions League last 16
A 2-0 defeat away at Swansea City
Leicester City.hint: Leicester lost the Champions League last-16 first leg 2-1 in Seville on 22 February 2017, and Ranieri was dismissed the following day — ten months after winning the Premier League.

Leicester City.q: Who was Leicester's manager for the Champions League quarter-final against Atlético Madrid in April 2017?
Leicester City.hint: Craig Shakespeare, Ranieri's assistant, was promoted after the Italian's sacking and led Leicester past Sevilla and into the quarter-final, which Atlético Madrid won 2-1 on aggregate.

Leicester City.q: Brendan Rodgers left which club to become Leicester manager in February 2019, replacing Claude Puel?
Leicester City.hint: Rodgers walked out on Celtic mid-season in February 2019, with the club well clear at the top of the Scottish Premiership, to take over from Claude Puel at Leicester.

Leicester City.q: Leicester won the FA Cup for the first time in their history in 2021, beating Chelsea 1-0 at Wembley. Who scored the winner?
Leicester City.hint: Youri Tielemans struck from distance into the top corner in the 63rd minute of the 2021 FA Cup final, ending a wait that had included four previous losing finals, the last of them in 1969.

Leicester City.q: Under Brendan Rodgers, Leicester reached the semi-finals of the first ever Europa Conference League in 2021-22. Which side knocked them out?
Leicester City.hint: José Mourinho's Roma won the semi-final 2-1 on aggregate, Tammy Abraham's header settling the second leg in Rome, and went on to win the inaugural final against Feyenoord.

Leicester City.q: Kasper Schmeichel joined Leicester in 2011 and stayed for eleven years. Which club did Leicester sign him from?
Leicester City.hint: Leicester signed Schmeichel from Leeds United in June 2011; Manchester City, Cardiff City and Notts County had all come earlier in his career.

Leicester City.q: Kasper Schmeichel finally left Leicester in the summer of 2022. Which club did he join?
Leicester City.hint: Schmeichel signed a three-year contract with Ligue 1 side Nice in August 2022, ending eleven years and more than 450 competitive appearances for Leicester.

Leicester City.q: Leicester signed the teenage centre-back Wesley Fofana in October 2020 from which club?
Leicester City.hint: Fofana arrived from Saint-Étienne in October 2020 aged 19, and two years later left for Chelsea for a reported £70m plus add-ons.

Leicester City.q: Harvey Barnes, a Leicester academy product, was sold for around £38m in July 2023 after relegation. Which club signed him?
Leicester City.hint: Newcastle United paid a reported £38m for Barnes in July 2023, weeks after he had scored 13 Premier League goals in Leicester's relegation season.

Leicester City.q: Who scored the 89th-minute penalty that won Leicester the 2021 Community Shield against Manchester City?
Leicester City.hint: Substitute Kelechi Iheanacho converted an 89th-minute penalty after being tripped by Nathan Aké, beating Manchester City — the club Leicester had signed him from in 2017.

Leicester City.q: Leicester were relegated on the final day of the 2022-23 Premier League season despite beating West Ham 2-1. Which club's win that same afternoon sent them down?
Leicester City.hint: Everton's 1-0 win over Bournemouth at Goodison Park lifted them to 36 points and left Leicester stranded in 18th on 34, relegated despite winning their own game.

Leicester City.q: Leicester's relegation in 2023 made them only the second club to have won the Premier League and later be relegated from it. Which club was the first?
Leicester City.hint: Blackburn Rovers won the Premier League in 1995 and went down in 1999; Leeds, Manchester City and Nottingham Forest were all English champions before the Premier League existed.

Leicester City.q: Leicester went straight back up as champions in 2023-24, finishing on 97 points. Which club finished second, a single point behind, and was promoted automatically with them?
Leicester City.hint: Ipswich Town finished second on 96 points to Leicester's 97, with Leeds United third on 90 and Southampton going up through the play-offs.

Leicester City.q: Enzo Maresca was appointed Leicester manager in June 2023, weeks after relegation. What job had he held immediately before taking it?
o: Manager of Manchester City's under-23 side
Assistant to Pep Guardiola at Manchester City
Assistant to Roberto Mancini with Italy
Leicester City.hint: Maresca had returned to Manchester City as one of Pep Guardiola's assistant managers in June 2022, following a short spell in charge of Parma, before Leicester appointed him on 16 June 2023.

Leicester City.q: Leicester paid a reported £1m for Jamie Vardy in 2012, then a record fee for a non-league player. Which club did they buy him from?
Leicester City.hint: Vardy joined Leicester in May 2012 from Fleetwood Town, who had just won the Conference Premier, having previously played for Stocksbridge Park Steels and FC Halifax Town.

Leicester City.q: Harry Maguire's £80m move from Leicester to Manchester United in 2019 made him the world's most expensive defender. Whose fee did it beat?
Leicester City.hint: Maguire's reported £80m fee in August 2019 overtook the £75m Liverpool had paid Southampton for Virgil van Dijk in January 2018 — and Leicester had bought Maguire from Hull City two years earlier.

Leicester City.q: Tottenham's 2-2 draw at Chelsea on 2 May 2016 confirmed Leicester as Premier League champions. Which Chelsea player scored the late equaliser that sealed it?
Leicester City.hint: Eden Hazard curled in an equaliser at Stamford Bridge with seven minutes left, after Gary Cahill had pulled one back, ending Tottenham's title hopes and crowning Leicester.

Leicester City.q: Jamie Vardy scored in 11 consecutive Premier League games during the 2015-16 season. Whose record did that run break?
Leicester City.hint: Vardy's goal against Manchester United in November 2015 was his 11th in a row, passing Ruud van Nistelrooy's 10-game run for Manchester United set in 2003.

Leicester City.q: Leicester paid around £1m for Jamie Vardy in 2012, then a record fee for a non-league player. Which club did they buy him from?
Leicester City.hint: Vardy joined from Fleetwood Town in May 2012, having previously played for Stocksbridge Park Steels and Halifax Town.

Leicester City.q: N'Golo Kanté was signed in the summer of 2015 for a reported £5.6m. Which French club did Leicester take him from?
Leicester City.hint: Kanté arrived from Caen in August 2015 and was sold to Chelsea a year later for around £32m.

Leicester City.q: Riyad Mahrez cost Leicester about £400,000 in January 2014, when they were still a Championship club. Which club did he join from?
Leicester City.hint: Mahrez was playing second-tier French football for Le Havre when Leicester signed him in January 2014.

Leicester City.q: In April 2016 Riyad Mahrez became the first African player to win which award?
o: PFA Players' Player of the Year
UEFA Men's Player of the Year
Leicester City.hint: Mahrez was voted PFA Players' Player of the Year for 2015-16, the first African player to take the award.

Leicester City.q: Claudio Ranieri was appointed Leicester manager in July 2015. Which team had he managed immediately before that?
Leicester City.hint: Ranieri's previous job was with the Greece national team, who sacked him in November 2014 after a home defeat by the Faroe Islands.

Leicester City.q: Ranieri promised his players pizza if they kept a clean sheet. Which side did Leicester shut out in October 2015 to earn it?
Leicester City.hint: Leicester's first clean sheet of 2015-16 came in a 1-0 win over Crystal Palace in October, after which Ranieri took the squad to a pizzeria to make their own.

Leicester City.q: Leicester sacked Ranieri in February 2017. Who took charge and led them past Sevilla into the Champions League quarter-finals weeks later?
Leicester City.hint: Assistant manager Craig Shakespeare stepped up after Ranieri's dismissal and oversaw the 2-0 second-leg win over Sevilla that sent Leicester through 3-2 on aggregate.

Leicester City.q: Who scored the goal that won Leicester the 2021 FA Cup final against Chelsea?
Leicester City.hint: Tielemans struck from distance in the 63rd minute at Wembley for the only goal of a 1-0 win that gave Leicester their first FA Cup.

Leicester City.q: Chelsea thought they had equalised in the closing minutes of the 2021 FA Cup final, only for VAR to rule the goal out. Who put the ball in the net?
Leicester City.hint: Ben Chilwell, a Leicester academy graduate, turned in a late rebound for Chelsea, but VAR ruled the goal out for offside.

Leicester City.q: The 1997 League Cup final went to a replay at Hillsborough after a 1-1 draw at Wembley. Who scored Leicester's extra-time winner in the replay?
Leicester City.hint: Steve Claridge's extra-time strike beat Middlesbrough 1-0 on 16 April 1997 and gave Leicester their first major trophy in 33 years.

Leicester City.q: Leicester beat Tranmere Rovers 2-1 in the 2000 League Cup final, the last one staged at the old Wembley. Who scored both of their goals?
Leicester City.hint: Captain and centre-back Matt Elliott headed both goals, each from a Steve Guppy corner, in the February 2000 win over Tranmere.

Leicester City.q: Leicester's last competitive match at Filbert Street, in May 2002, finished 2-1 against Tottenham. Who scored their final goal at the old ground?
Leicester City.hint: Academy graduate Matt Piper headed the winner on 11 May 2002, the last goal scored at Filbert Street after 111 years of football there.

Leicester City.q: Leicester left Filbert Street in 2002, the year they were relegated from the Premier League. What was their new stadium called when it opened?
Leicester City.hint: The ground opened in 2002 as the Walkers Stadium, named after the Leicester crisp company, and became the King Power Stadium in 2011.

Leicester City.q: Gary Lineker left Leicester in the summer of 1985 for £800,000. Which club did he join?
Leicester City.hint: Lineker joined reigning champions Everton in 1985, and only moved on to Barcelona a year later.

Leicester City.q: Leicester sold Peter Shilton in November 1974 for £325,000, then a world record for a goalkeeper. Which club signed him?
Leicester City.hint: Shilton went to Stoke City — the same club Leicester had sold Gordon Banks to in 1967 to make room for the teenage Shilton.

Leicester City.q: Leicester played in the third tier for the first time in their history in 2008-09. Who managed them straight back up as League One champions?
Leicester City.hint: Nigel Pearson took over in the summer of 2008 and won the League One title at the first attempt, including a club-record 23-game unbeaten league run.

q.q: Olympiacos signed the Brazilian playmaker Giovanni in the summer of 1999. Which club did they buy him from?
q.hint: Giovanni joined Olympiacos from Barcelona in 1999, three years after the Catalans had signed him from Santos.

q.q: Riyad Mahrez cost Leicester about £400,000 in January 2014, when they were still a Championship club. Which club did he join from?
q.hint: Leicester plucked him out of Ligue 2, from the port-city side founded in 1872 and generally reckoned the oldest football club in France.

q.q: Olympiacos hired Pedro Martins in 2018 from which Portuguese club?
q.hint: He arrived in Piraeus after two seasons in the Minho, having taken that side to a Taça de Portugal final in 2017; at Olympiacos he went on to win three straight Greek titles.

q.q: Vasilis Torosidis left Olympiacos in January 2013 to join which Italian club?
q.hint: The Greek right-back headed for a club in the Italian capital, and only left three and a half seasons later when Bologna signed him in 2016.

q.q: Predrag Djordjevic played 13 seasons at Olympiacos between 1996 and 2009. How many Greek championships did he collect?
q.hint: Twelve, from thirteen attempts. Olympiacos won the title every season Djordjevic was there apart from 2003-04, when Panathinaikos pipped them by two points.

q.q: From which German club did Olympiacos sign Kostas Fortounis in 2014?
q.hint: He spent three seasons with the Red Devils of the Fritz-Walter-Stadion, who were in the 2. Bundesliga by the time he left for Piraeus.

q.q: Olympiacos' run of seven straight championships began in 1996-97, and one manager delivered the first three before leaving in November 1999. Who was he?
q.hint: Dusan Bajevic crossed from AEK Athens in June 1996 and won the 1996-97, 1997-98 and 1998-99 titles - the first of them Olympiacos' first championship in ten years. He departed in November 1999, and a succession of coaches carried the run on to a seventh title in 2003.

q.q: Stelios Giannakopoulos won the Greek championship in all seven of his seasons at Olympiacos, from 1996-97 to 2002-03, then left in May 2003 for which Premier League club?
q.hint: Sam Allardyce signed him on 28 May 2003, a year before he won Euro 2004 with Greece, and he stayed at the Reebok until he was released in 2008.

q.q: Who captained Olympiacos in the 2024 UEFA Europa Conference League final and lifted the trophy?
q.hint: Kostas Fortounis, Olympiacos captain since August 2018, started the final with the armband in the 1-0 extra-time win over Fiorentina.

q.q: N'Golo Kanté was signed in the summer of 2015 for a reported £5.6m. Which French club did Leicester take him from?
q.hint: He had helped the club win promotion from Ligue 2 in 2014 and played one Ligue 1 season there before Leicester moved; a year after arriving he was a Premier League champion, and Chelsea paid around £32m for him.

q.q: Chelsea thought they had equalised in the closing minutes of the 2021 FA Cup final, only for VAR to chalk the goal off. Which Chelsea player was ruled offside in the build-up?
q.hint: Thiago Silva's cross-field ball picked out Ben Chilwell — a Leicester academy graduate — and VAR judged him offside by the finest of margins, so the scrambled finish that followed did not stand.

q.q: In the last-16 second leg against Sevilla in March 2017, Kasper Schmeichel gave away a penalty and then saved it. Which Sevilla player did he deny from the spot?
q.hint: Schmeichel rushed out and caught Vitolo to concede the penalty — and was booked for it — before smothering Steven N'Zonzi's tame spot-kick, protecting the 2-0 win that took Leicester through 3-2 on aggregate.

q.q: Claudio Ranieri was sacked by Leicester in February 2017, less than 24 hours after which match?
o: A 1-0 FA Cup defeat at Millwall
A 2-1 defeat away at Sevilla in the Champions League last 16
A 2-0 defeat away at Swansea City
q.hint: Leicester lost the Champions League last-16 first leg 2-1 in Seville on 22 February 2017, and Ranieri was dismissed the following evening with the club a point above the relegation zone — nine months after winning the Premier League.
